# Catalog expansion and Austin lifestyle planner

Historical release 0.6.0 notes. Superseded by [release 0.7.0 Austin calibration](austin-calibration.md).

The catalog contains 26 broad pathways, 79 college fields of study, and 62 specific careers. Fields are editorial study possibilities, not an institutional program list or CIP–SOC crosswalk. The original eight pathway IDs and version-1 browser drafts remain compatible. New pathways add transparent editorial interest-theme links. The assessment analysis version is 1.1.0; financial metrics do not enter that analysis.

Every pathway, field, and occupation has education, requirements, education costs/aid, and earnings context. An explicit unknown is part of coverage, not evidence that a cost or requirement is zero. Undergraduate budgets do not stand in for graduate/professional credential costs. Costs still require a named college/training provider, program, year, residency, period, enrollment and living assumptions. Plans can link any of the three catalog types. Association groups are collapsible and scroll independently.

The new training entries include electricians, plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, automotive repair, EMT, chefs/head cooks, and dental assisting, alongside the existing tattoo exploration. Formal occupational training, apprenticeship, employer experience, certifications and licenses are distinguished from optional college study. Chef wages describe an experienced occupation, and EMT wages are not paramedic wages. Aid eligibility requires checking both institution and program. Apprentice pay is not imputed from the occupation median.

## Earnings provenance

The 53 added wage records were read from BLS May 2025 national employee wage tables through O*NET OnLine. `data-sources/catalog-wages.json` retains their 25th percentile, median and 75th percentile. Each rendered occupation carries its specific source URL, period, geography, currency, population and exclusions. `catalog-education.json` retains the 53 BLS Handbook education-source references. Nutrition also links CDR credential eligibility; HVAC links EPA certification guidance. Legal eligibility still requires the intended jurisdiction.

The tattoo-specific gap stays unfilled. Employee percentiles are not translated to experience years, starting pay, or self-employed profit. Official O*NET task, knowledge, skill, ability and interest links are present for every occupation. These are external exploration resources, not a student aptitude score.

## Austin lifestyle calculation

`#/lifestyle` is an educational cash-flow illustration. Each career links to `#/lifestyle/<career-id>`, initially using its national median if available. A user can select the 25th percentile, median, 75th percentile, custom gross pay, or manual take-home. No Austin wage premium or discount is invented. Income and expense assumptions persist locally; a general report does not include them. Explicit lifestyle exports and full-draft backups do include them.

The estimate assumes a single nondependent employee under age 50, standard deduction, traditional employee retirement plan, ordinary wages only, Social Security/Medicare coverage and no credits. It uses IRS 2026 marginal brackets, $16,100 standard deduction, $184,500 Social Security wage cap, 6.2% employee Social Security and 1.45% Medicare plus the 0.9% additional Medicare tax above $200,000. Deferrals above the assumed $24,500 employee plan limit require review rather than silently reducing tax. Health costs are subtracted after tax. Manual take-home bypasses the tax calculation and avoids deducting retirement/health twice. Self-employment requires a separately supplied personal take-home figure; business revenue is not salary.

Housing, transport, essentials, debt, savings, dining, travel, recreation and clothing share one reconciled monthly ledger. A negative balance stays negative. Discretionary story cards describe selected spending, not extra purchasing power; a shortfall labels them as a wish list. Item and trip counts are budget equivalents, not promises or bookable products. A zero target produces no divided count.

Housing ownership includes amortized principal/interest, property tax, insurance, HOA, maintenance reserve and utilities. The separate upfront target includes down payment, an assumed 3% closing allowance and six months of entered essentials. PMI is not estimated; low down payments explicitly require adding a lender quote. Actual parcel taxes, exemptions, underwriting, property availability and price appreciation are not inferred. Vehicle calculations include financing and operating expenses; down payment is separate and a paid-off vehicle still has operating costs.

All price presets are editable invented scenarios, not local market averages or product quotes. Brand and vehicle names illustrate shopping/vehicle types, with no salary-to-status assignment. The sourced local reference is HUD FY 2027 Austin–Round Rock–San Marcos Fair Market Rent, page 45: $1,530 one-bedroom and $1,817 two-bedroom gross monthly rent. These program benchmarks include typical tenant-paid utilities, and are not asking-rent averages. FY 2027 was verified on the current HUD source page and Austin does not appear in its listed reevaluation exceptions. The reference does not populate a base-rent input and add utilities a second time. CapMetro's $41.25 local monthly fare is dated October 2026 and the UI notes the announced January 10, 2027 fare change.

The wage period (2025), tax year (2026), HUD fiscal period (2027), and editable price assumptions remain labeled separately and are not inflation-adjusted. This is present-dollar exploration rather than a forecast of the student's life after graduation.

## Validation

53 automated tests cover all catalog records, complete panels, preserved unknowns, training/graduate distinctions, taxonomy links, filtering, migration, privacy, marginal taxes, amortization, full cost reconciliation, ownership upfront costs, manual take-home, zero targets and invalid inputs, plus existing assessment and finance regression checks. Browser verification covers catalog filtering, field and career pages, career-to-lifestyle links, assumption changes, shortfalls, zero-rate mortgages, persistence and export. Desktop and narrow-screen layouts are checked through the browser.
